papers:
  - lead: Gabriele Vilkaite
    photo: members/images/round/gabi.jpg
    page: members/gabri.html
    journal: bioRxiv
    date: "Oct 23, 2026"
    title: "A coordinated and reproducible multicellular response to AD pathology"
    url: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.19.759610
    summary: "Single-cell studies of the Alzheimer's brain often report differing results and rarely
      consider how cell types respond together. Across 2.3 million nuclei from 427 ROSMAP donors, we
      identified multicellular signatures of AD pathology and of sex, including profound changes in
      RORB-GABRG excitatory neurons and disrupted oligodendrocyte precursor signalling. These
      signatures predicted neuropathology and sex in a fully independent dataset (SEA-AD), giving a
      baseline against which perturbation and treatment experiments can be compared."
    figure: images/news/vilkaite2026_workflow.jpg
    alt: "Overview of the analysis workflow, from single-cell data to robust gene clusters"
    credit: "Figure from this paper (CC BY-NC 4.0)."

  - lead: Jonathan Rittmo
    photo: members/images/round/jon.jpg
    page: members/jon.html
    journal: Nature Neuroscience
    date: "Oct 1, 2026"
    title: "Different functional connectivity gradients reflect aging and Alzheimer's disease"
    url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41593-026-02402-0
    summary: "In two independent cohorts (BioFINDER-2, N = 973; ADNI, N = 129), functional connectivity
      changes linked to aging and to Alzheimer's disease aligned with separate axes of brain
      communication. Early AD pathology and later cognitive decline followed the sensory-association
      axis, while age-related change followed the representation-executive axis across the adult
      lifespan."
    figure: images/news/rittmo2026_axes.jpg
    alt: "Brain maps and scatter plots relating age and AD pathology to the sensory-association and representation-executive axes"
    credit: "Figure from this paper."

  - lead: Lijun An
    photo: members/images/round/lijun.jpg
    page: members/lijun.html
    journal: Nature Medicine
    date: "Mar 31, 2026"
    title: "A deep joint-learning proteomics model for diagnosis of six conditions associated with dementia"
    url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-026-04303-y
    summary: "Mixed pathologies make dementia hard to diagnose, and scalable biomarkers are missing for most of
      them. We present ProtAIDe-Dx, a deep joint-learning model trained on 17,187 patients and controls that
      uses plasma proteomics to diagnose six conditions at once, with a balanced accuracy of 70-95%. It
      improved differential diagnosis in a memory clinic sample and shows which proteins drive each
      person's result, all from a single blood draw."
    figure: images/news/an2026_workflow.jpg
    alt: "Workflow of the ProtAIDe-Dx model, from plasma proteins through a neural network to disease probabilities and an individual risk report"
    credit: "Adapted from this paper, panel a of a main figure (CC BY 4.0)."

  - lead: Jacob Vogel
    photo: members/images/round/jake.jpg
    page: members/jake.html
    journal: Nature Medicine
    date: "Apr 29, 2021"
    title: "Four distinct trajectories of tau deposition identified in Alzheimer's disease"
    url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-021-01309-6
    summary: "Using tau-PET scans from 1,612 individuals, we identified four distinct trajectories of tau
      pathology: limbic, MTL-sparing, posterior and lateral temporal. These subtypes were stable over
      follow-up, replicated in a separate sample with a different radiotracer, and showed distinct
      demographic and cognitive profiles and outcomes, suggesting a re-examination of the idea of
      'typical' Alzheimer's disease."
    figure: images/news/vogel2021_subtypes.jpg
    alt: "Brain maps of tau in the limbic, MTL-sparing, posterior and lateral temporal subtypes, with a plot of how individuals fall across the four subtypes"
    credit: "Adapted from this paper."

  - lead: Jacob Vogel
    photo: members/images/round/jake.jpg
    page: members/jake.html
    journal: Nature Communications
    date: "May 26, 2020"
    title: "Spread of pathological tau proteins through communicating neurons in human Alzheimer's disease"
    url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15701-2
    summary: "Animal models suggest that tau spreads from cell to cell through neuronal connections. We tested
      this in 312 people along the Alzheimer's continuum using an epidemic spreading model, which explained
      up to 70% of the variance in the spatial pattern of tau. Our results provide evidence in humans that
      tau spreads through neuronal communication pathways, and that beta-amyloid accelerates this process."
    figure: images/news/vogel2020_esm_patterns.jpg
    alt: "Brain maps comparing the expected and observed patterns of tau with the patterns predicted by the epidemic spreading model"
    credit: "Figure from this paper (CC BY 4.0)."

```{r cards, echo=FALSE}
# Builds one card per paper from the `papers` list above.
library(htmltools)

papers <- rmarkdown::metadata$papers

card <- function(p) {
  tags$article(
    class = "pub-card",
    tags$figure(class = "pub-figure", img(src = p$figure, alt = p$alt, loading = "lazy")),
    div(class = "pub-body",
        div(class = "pub-credit", p$credit),
        div(class = "pub-head",
            div(div(class = "pub-lead", paste(p$lead, "et al.")),
                div(class = "pub-journal", p$journal),
                div(class = "pub-date", p$date)),
            a(href = p$page, img(class = "pub-photo", src = p$photo, alt = p$lead, loading = "lazy"))),
        h2(class = "pub-title", a(href = p$url, target = "_blank", p$title)),
        tags$p(class = "pub-summary", p$summary),
        a(class = "pub-link", href = p$url, target = "_blank", "Read the paper")))
}

div(class = "pub-grid", lapply(papers, card))
```

:::
